review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the supporting simp lemmas in MultiWord.lean, WordScheduling.lean, SlotAssembly.lean, PiTensor.lean and SparseShear.lean. I also searched the FourierCircuit directory for other uses of the `simp [..., Word.weight]` pattern. I did not run Lean, so the replacement lemmas are untested suggestions. I considered making `RawPrice.tensor`, `directSum`, `power` and `reindex` simp lemmas. I rejected that because they carry `IsUnit` side conditions, and their uses are explicit `rw` calls with supplied unit proofs. The `@[simp]` lemmas on `Word.Pure` and `purePower` looked consistent. The two findings below are the strongest, and I am unsure how much of the long simp set at line 150 the proposed lemma would remove.

findings.declaration: ExactFourier.Packing.RawPrice.word_le / reindex_le / mul_le / tensor_le / directSum_le / embedded_le (uses of simp with Word.weight)
findings.problem: The simp set has no lemma computing the weight of a single `callWord`. `Word.weight_nil`, `weight_cons_call`, `weight_append`, `weight_embed` and `weight_reindex` are all simp lemmas, and `calls_callWord` and `matrix_callWord` exist for `callWord`. There is no `weight_callWord`. As a result, `simpa [W,Word.weight]` (also at lines 76, 129, 167 and 279, and in other files) unfolds the definition `Word.weight` into `(W.calls.map p).sum` and then relies on `calls_callWord` and `List.map` simp lemmas. This unfolding competes with the existing `Word.weight_append` rules, which are stated on `Word.weight`. It also needs `W`, `V` and `A` passed as let-unfolding arguments.
findings.proposed_change: Add next to `calls_callWord` in MultiWord.lean (or WordScheduling.lean) a lemma `@[simp] theorem Word.weight_callWord (p : τ → ℝ) (t : τ) (e : D t ↪ α) : (callWord (A := A) t e).weight p = p t`. It can be proved by `simp [Word.weight]` or `rfl`. Then replace `Word.weight` in these simp calls by `W`, `V`, `A` only, so `Word.weight` stays folded. Do the same for `monoWord` (weight 0) if needed.
findings.benefit: The call sites use only the folded `Word.weight` normal form, which already has the `weight_append` and `weight_embed` simp lemmas. Proofs no longer depend on how `Word.weight` is implemented. About six call sites in this file, and others in RawPositive.lean and FiniteSeparation.lean, shrink and become more robust.

findings.problem: The proof simplifies `hh` by unfolding twelve definitions, including the interface definitions `pairPrice`, `speciesPrice`, `SpeciesDomain`, `callWord`, `Word.calls` and `Step.kind`. It then needs the fragile `convert hh using 1 ; congr 1` to match the goal. This means the simp interface has no lemmas for `pairPrice` on a pair of `some` species or for the weight of a call word. The proof depends on the exact unfolded shape and cannot be reused for similar cases. The related `pairPrice_map` in ComparisonRename.lean also has to work through the cardinalities by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma for the common case, for example `pairPrice_some_some (v : τ → ℝ) (s t : τ) (h) : pairPrice (D := D) v ⟨(some s, some t), h⟩ = Fintype.card (D t) * v s + Fintype.card (D s) * v t`, plus the `Word.weight_callWord` lemma from the previous finding. Then `rw` or `simp only [pairPrice_some_some, Word.weight_callWord]` replaces the twelve-definition unfold. The branch with `q.1.1 = some (some false)` and `q.1.2 = some (some true)` then reduces to `biMatrix`/`BiDomain` cardinality facts and no longer needs `convert ... congr 1`.
findings.benefit: This avoids the unwanted wholesale unfolding of definitions that have their own simp lemmas (`speciesWord_count` and `Word.weight_*`). The proof no longer depends on `convert`, and other proofs about `pairPrice` can use the same lemma.
